correctness.rationale: Properness makes each row and column rainbow, so a neighborhood color has odd multiplicity exactly when it belongs to exactly one of the incident row and column color sets. This criterion gives the rectangular upper bound immediately. In the square case it excludes n colors, and for n+1 colors the row-omission and column-omission counts for each color are equal because both count the same total occurrences; a common omitted color therefore forces a failing cell. The cyclic Z_(n+2) construction has proper rows and columns and omission pairs of different cyclic gap types, so it is odd. Small exhaustive enumeration and direct construction replay corroborate every step.

value.rationale: Rook graphs are a canonical family simultaneously realized as Cartesian products of complete graphs, line graphs of complete bipartite graphs, and in the square case two-dimensional Hamming graphs. The result shows a sharp square-versus-rectangular transition: when m<n, the odd constraint costs nothing beyond ordinary coloring and every optimum works, while at m=n it costs exactly two colors. The row/column omission-balance proof gives a structural explanation and an explicit all-order construction, making the result useful beyond a one-off computation.
